value.body: A two-year master's in one area of forestry, such as silviculture and agroforestry, tree improvement, forest products and utilisation, wildlife science or natural resource management. It combines coursework with a research thesis and leads to research, teaching, consultancy and scientist roles.

items.label: Postgraduate students in forestry
items.note: All master's-level programmes in the forestry discipline, from institutions that reported

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc Forestry (some programmes also accept agriculture or life-science graduates). Admission is through ICAR's all-India PG entrance (AICE-JRF/SRF) for agricultural universities, or a university or institute's own entrance test.

value.title: At a glance
items: A master's is required for the ICAR scientist exam (ARS) and is usual for research posts.
Forestry research institutes and environmental consultancies hire for project and research roles.
Many graduates go on to a PhD with a fellowship.

value.title: Postgraduate students in Forestry
value.note: Agriculture group, 'Forestry' row. The rise in 2023-24 is large for a small field and may partly reflect more institutions reporting or reclassification. AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 13, postgraduate level, actual responses (Ministry of Education)
